question: A tradesman marks his goods at 26% above the cost price. He allows his customer a discount of 12% on the marked price. His profit per cent is:
solution:
**Given:**

A tradesman marks his goods at 26% above the cost price. 

He allows his customer a discount of 12% on the marked price

**Formula used:**

P% = [(SP - CP)/CP] × 100

SP = MP(1 - D%)

**Calculations:**

Let the CP of goods be Rs. 100

According to the question,

Marked price = 100(1 + 26%)

⇒ MP = 100(1.26) = Rs. 126

Now for SP

SP = 126(1 - 12%) 

⇒ SP = 126(1 - 0.12)

⇒ SP = 126(0.88) = Rs. 110.88

Now his profit%

P% = [(110.88 - 100)/100] × 100

⇒ P% = [(10.88)/100] × 100 = 10.88%

**∴ Profit % of trademen will be 10.88%. **
